insight.title: The Relatable Performance
insight.subtitle: We crave connection online, but influencers profit from making staged lives feel intimately familiar.
insight.notificationHook: Your online friend? That's a job.

sections.text: Influencers masterfully craft the illusion of everyday life, sharing "authentic" moments that feel deeply personal. They’re just like us, right? Cooking, struggling, laughing – all on brand.
But this "authenticity" is a highly polished, strategic performance. Every "candid" moment, every "spontaneous" revelation, is often meticulously planned and optimized for engagement metrics.

We consume these manufactured realities, blurring the line between genuine connection and professional content. Our digital "friends" are actually skilled marketers, selling both products and an aspirational, yet fake, closeness.
The parasocial loop: it’s real, it’s fake, it’s revenue.
